st: Soak the rinsed rice in warm salted water while you cook the meat.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over high heat until shimmering. Brown the lamb on all sides.
Add the onions and cook until deep golden.
Add the carrots, [[1 tbsp]] cumin seeds and [[2 tsp]] salt, and cook until the carrots soften.
Pour in [[1 cup]] boiling water, cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the meat. Do not stir.
Pour [[2.5 cups]] boiling water gently down the side, nestle in the garlic head, and cook on high until the water is level with the rice.
Make small holes in the rice with a spoon handle, cover tightly, and steam on the lowest heat until tender. Mix gently and serve.
Put the lamb in a pot with [[6 cups]] water, bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add [[1.5 tsp]] salt, cover and simmer until the lamb is very tender.
Lift out the meat, remove the bones and chop the meat into small pieces. Keep the broth hot.
Tear the bread into small pieces and pile on a large dish.
Scatter the meat, raw onions and tomatoes over the bread.
Ladle enough hot broth over to soften the bread without making it soupy.
Sprinkle generously with black pepper and herbs.
Serve right away with extra broth on the side.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and water into a soft dough, knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Mix the lamb, onions, [[1 tsp]] salt and pepper for the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) with a baking sheet inside. The sand-baking method is replaced by a hot oven.
Divide the dough in two and roll each thin into a large round.
Spread the filling evenly over one round.
Cover with the second round and press the edges together to seal.
Brush the top with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and prick a few times with a fork.
Bake until golden and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C). Brush with the remaining butter, slice and serve with yogurt.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and water into a stiff dough. Knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Combine the lamb, onions, pumpkin, [[1 tsp]] salt and pepper for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into squares.
Spoon filling into the center of each square.
Bring up the corners, pinch the edges to seal into a closed parcel.
Grease the steamer tiers with oil and arrange the manti so they do not touch.
Steam over boiling water until the dough is tender and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
Serve with melted butter and a spoonful of yogurt.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and water and rest until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl, add the yeast mixture and [[2 tbsp]] butter, and knead into a soft dough.
Cover and let it rise until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Divide the dough into four balls and flatten each into a round with a thicker rim.
Press the center with a fork to make small holes.
Bake each on the hot stone until golden brown.
Brush with the remaining butter and serve warm.
Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt and water into a soft dough, knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion, lamb if using, and pumpkin until soft and the meat is fully cooked.
Add the spinach and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and cook until wilted. Cool the filling.
Divide the dough into eight pieces and roll each very thin into a round.
Put filling on half of each round.
Fold over into a half-moon and press the edges to seal.
Cook each in a dry hot skillet until blistered and golden on both sides.
Brush with melted butter and serve hot.
Put the lamb in a large pot with [[8 cups]] cold water and bring to a boil.
Skim off the foam that rises.
Add the onions, [[2 tsp]] salt and pepper. Cover and simmer on low until the lamb is tender.
Add the carrots and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and bell pepper.
Cook until all the vegetables are soft.
Taste and adjust the salt. Lift out the lamb, pull the meat off the bones and return it to the pot.
Ladle into bowls and top with cilantro.
Mix the flour, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and water into a firm dough, knead until smooth and rest, covered.
Mix the lamb, onions, cumin, pepper, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] melted butter for the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Roll the dough thin and cut into squares about the size of your palm.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each square.
Fold into triangles and pinch the edges tightly to seal.
Place on the sheet, brush with egg and butter, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake until golden and the filling reaches 160°F (71°C).
